Olivia (Finance): FYI — we just received an inbound EUR SWIFT into our DEIB Chase EUR account, amount €12,430.72, value date 2026-03-09. Sender shows 'Volt Systems GmbH' but the remittance/narrative is blank and the bank ref is partial `UVX746` which doesn't match any invoice or PO in NetSuite.
Raj (Support): Can you paste the bank's booking reference + any UETR/txn id? If there's an image of the bank advice, drop it here. We'll need to ask the customer for an MT103 if bank can't provide more.
Olivia (Finance): Bank booking id: `20260309CHK987654`. Receiving acct credited CHASDEEURXXX. Payer name exactly as shown: Volt Systems GmbH. No remit text. I attached the trans screenshot and the raw transaction line from the feed.
Mei (Customer Success): I'll reach out to the customer now. @Luca can you ask them to provide: 1) payment advice/confirmation, 2) full MT103/MT202, 3) ordering account IBAN + value date + any internal reference. Use the template below.
Mei (Customer Success): Template I sent (short): "Hi — thanks for the payment. We're seeing an unsupported/missing reference on the inbound wire (€12,430.72 on 2026-03-09). Can you share the bank payment advice or full MT103 and confirm which invoice/PO this payment was for? If you can't get MT103, please confirm ordering account (IBAN), sending bank, and any contract number."
Alex (Treasury): In parallel we should open a bank trace. If the counterparty bank can provide the MT103 we can reconcile quickly. I'll open a trace ticket with Chase.
payments-bot: Trace ticket created: `TR-20260309-44` — please attach MT103 when available.
Raj (Support): Alex — for the trace the bank usually wants: amount, value date, receiving acct, our receiving booking ref, sender name, and ordering account if known. Suggest including this snippet in the request:

```
Please investigate an incoming credit to our Chase EUR account credited 2026-03-09 for EUR 12,430.72.
Our receiving account: CHASDEEURXXX
Our booking reference: 20260309CHK987654
Sender provided name: Volt Systems GmbH
Sender reference on banded field: UVX746 (truncated)
Please supply MT103/ordering customer details and ordering bank to help reconcile.
```

Olivia (Finance): Done — filed with Chase support (case #CH-88921). They said they'll try to obtain MT103 from the sending bank but it can take 24-72h.
Mei (Customer Success): Customer replied: they initiated payment from Volt clearing pool account (IBAN DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31), they thought it was for a subscription but can't find their invoice ID. They've attached a PDF payment confirmation (no MT103).
Alex (Treasury): If they can't provide MT103, ask for the ordering account IBAN + value date + exact send amount and any internal invoice/contract reference. With ordering IBAN and our trace ticket Chase can often map it.
Mei (Customer Success): Sent follow-up asking specifically for the ordering account name/IBAN + the exact send timestamp and SWIFT ordering bank.
Olivia (Finance): Quick note — if we can't match within 7 business days we hold it as unidentified credit per policy and open accounting suspense. But let's avoid that if possible.
payments-bot: Update on TR-20260309-44: bank responded, partial MT103 received (ordering customer details present but narrative blank). Ordering IBAN: DE44 5001 0517 5407 3249 31; ordering customer name: Volt Systems GmbH.
Mei (Customer Success): Customer confirms the payment was intended as a prepayment for PO-8841 (they referenced an internal contract number 2025-07 in their email). Not our invoice ID but matches the PO.
Olivia (Finance): Matched to PO-8841 as advance payment and applied to customer account. Reconciled and closed case. Marking the trace ticket resolved.
Raj (Support): Nice — thanks team. Can we add a quick KB note with the trace template and customer request wording so CS/Finance use the same script next time?
Alex (Treasury): I'll drop a short snippet in Confluence under Finance > Wire reconciliation templates.
Mei (Customer Success): I'll follow up with the customer to confirm allocation and send a receipt. :white_check_mark:
